title: Hybrid µCT-FMT imaging and image analysis
protocol: Prepare a solution of 200 ml water, 2 % agarose, 1.8 g TiO2 powder, and 50 μl trypan blue.
Boil the prepared solution.
Fill the boiled solution into a rectangular form measuring approximately 8 cm in length, 3 cm in width, and 1.5 cm in height.
Create several fluorescent inclusions in the phantom using pipette tips containing a mix of fluorescence and µCT contrast agent.
Cut the pipette tips to prepare for creating the inclusions.
Seal the cut pipette tips with a lighter.
Place the mouse on chlorophyll-free food 7 days before imaging.
Initiate anesthesia by placing the mouse in a chamber filled with 2 % isoflurane in air (flow rate 5 L/min).
Confirm proper anesthetization by gentle toe or skin pinching and checking relaxation of muscle tonus.
Sustain the anesthesia using a tube placed on the nose of the mouse (2 % isoflurane in air, flow rate 1 L/min).
Apply vet ointment on anesthetized mice to prevent eye dryness.
Fix the anesthetized mouse on a heating pad using tape.
Place a catheter to the tail vein for injection.
Inject the fluorescent contrast agent into the tail vein.
Shave or depilate the scanning area in advance if necessary.
Monitor mice for skin changes after hair removal treatment.
Test tolerance of new mouse strains with hair removal cream on a small number of animals.
Keep the mouse anesthetized during imaging (2% isoflurane in air, flow rate 1 L/min).
Clean the multimodal mouse bed with wet tissues before use.
Attach the anesthetic gas tube to the mouse bed and fixate it with tape.
Place the anesthetized mouse into the mouse bed.
Ensure the head of the mouse is at the front indicator of the mouse bed.
Place the mouse in the middle of the mouse bed to optimize field of view usage.
Close the mouse bed and tighten the screws until the mouse is tightly held.
Monitor the mouse's thoracic breathing movements to ensure steady breathing.
Detach the long tube from the mouse bed and attach it to the connector outside the µCT.
Attach the remaining free end of the tube to the connector inside the µCT.
Drive the mouse bed into the µCT, ensuring the gas tube is not loose or caught by the rotating gantry.
If necessary, fixate the gas tube with tape.
Insert the tube into the cut-out of the holder on the mouse bed.
Close the µCT and acquire a topogram.
Select at least two subscans to cover a substantial part of the mouse and the mouse bed.
Select the µCT scan protocol named HQD-6565-360-90.
Operate tubes at 65 kV voltage and 1.0 mA current.
Alternatively, select scanning protocol SQD-6565-360-29 for reduced radiation dose and duration.
Start the µCT scan.
Do not open the lid during scanning to protect from radiation.
When scanning is completed, open the lid of the µCT scanner.
Reconnect the anesthetic tube after opening the lid.
Detach the mouse bed from the holder.
Transport the mouse bed to the FMT for imaging.
Turn on the anesthetic gas supply (2% isoflurane in air, flow rate 1 L/min) before placing the mouse into the FMT.
Create a study group with an appropriate number of subjects using the FMT control software.
Select the probes that will be used for imaging, including OsteoSense.
Carry the multimodal mouse bed with the mouse to the FMT.
Remove the anesthetic gas tube before inserting the mouse bed into the FMT.
Place the mouse bed into the FMT with the red indicator first (“head-first”).
Close the FMT.
Select the correct study group and subject in the FMT software.
Select the required channel of the FMT (for OsteoSense 750EX, use the 750 nm channel).
Add a description, e.g., “up” or “down”.
Acquire an overview scan by pressing “Capture”.
Adjust the imaging parameters for the 3D scan.
Enlarge the field of view to include as much as possible of the mouse.
Click “Advanced” and check the imaging settings.
Set sampling density to 3 mm, sensitivity to normal, and illumination min/max to 5000 and 50000, respectively.
Click “add to reconstruction queue” and then click “Scan” to start the FMT scan.
Wait for the FMT scan to complete, which takes approximately 5 to 15 minutes based on mouse size and thickness.
Flip the mouse bed including the mouse upside down after the initial scan is completed.
Acquire another scan with the mouse in its flipped position.
Monitor the mouse until it regains sufficient consciousness to walk around or maintain sternal recumbency post-anesthesia.
Create a folder for the study upon completion of µCT-FMT scans.
For each µCT-FMT scan, create one subfolder named with the mouse ID and time point.
Export FMT scans (up and down) as .fmt files.
Save each .fmt file into a subfolder with filenames ending in “_up.fmt” or “_down.fmt”.
Create a µCT reconstruction with isotropic voxel size 35 μm using the µCT software.
Select a smooth reconstruction kernel (T10).
Adjust the field of view to cover the entire mouse bed including markers.
Choose MIFX/RAW as output format and start the reconstruction.
Move the µCT reconstruction files into the subfolder of the µCT-FMT scan.
Export the µCT and FMT data for all scans.
Ensure each subfolder contains two .fmt files (up and down) and a µCT reconstruction in MIFX/RAW format.
Select Menu->CT-FMT->Check Completeness using Imalytics Preclinical software.
Fix any errors such as missing .fmt files or µCT reconstructions until no errors remain.
Using Menu->CT-FMT->Settings to check the server name of the Definiens software.
Adjust the server name if necessary.
Click Menu->CT-FMT->Fuse group in the Imalytics Preclinical software to perform automated µCT-FMT fusion for the entire study.
This process takes a few minutes per µCT-FMT scan and results in a folder with suffix “Package” parallel to the study folder.
Click Menu->CT-FMT->Reconstruct group (FMT) in the Imalytics Preclinical software to perform the fluorescence reconstruction including generation of absorption and scattering maps.
Each reconstruction requires 1 to 4 hours depending on the size of the mouse.
Store results in the package folder.
Load a µCT file as underlay and the fluorescence file as overlay.
Press “3D” to turn on the volume rendering and inspect the data set.
Click Menu->Classes->Add class and create a class named “tmp”.
Perform a thresholding operation to segment all regions with low intensity in the µCT data set (click Menu->Segmentation->Thresholding->Below and enter 600).
Create a “Lung” class.
Perform a “Fill Region” operation (right-click into the lung and select Menu->Fill Region->Fill region unlimited) to separate the lung from the outer air.
Delete the tmp class because it is not needed anymore.
Press F1 to delete all scribbles.
Using the computer mouse, draw scribbles to delineate the boundaries of the bladder.
Press F3 to fill the region enclosed by the scribbles with a temporary mask which appears as red overlay.
Iteratively add more scribbles (in any slicing orientation) and press F3 until a sufficient accuracy is achieved.
Typically, scribbles in 10 slices are sufficient.
Press F4 to store the temporary mask as “Bladder”.
Create a “Bone” class in the segmentation software.
Select ContextMenu->Thresholding->Above to perform a thresholding operation to classify all bright voxels (e.g., above 1,600) as “Bone”.
Perform cutting operations by iteratively drawing scribbles and pressing F2 to separate the spine from other skeletal parts.
Create a class “Spine” in the segmentation software.
Right-click into the spine and select ContextMenu->Fill Region->Fill region unlimited to perform a region filling operation on the spine.
Save the segmentation as a file inside the subfolder of the µCT-FMT scan with a consistent name, e.g., organs.seg.
Select Menu->Statistics->Class statistics (overlay) to generate a spreadsheet containing mean fluorescence intensity, volume and total amount for each class.
Click Menu->Batch->Set batch settings and then click Menu->Batch->Batch statistics to generate a single spreadsheet containing values for all regions of all µCT-FMT scans.
Probe Calibration
Scan µCT-FMT phantoms containing different known amounts of the probe (e.g., 100 pmol, 50 pmol, 25 pmol, and 0 pmol) as described in sections 4 and 5.
Perform up and down scans for each phantom using FMT.
Export the scanned data from the phantoms.
Fuse and reconstruct the exported data according to section 6 instructions.
Segment the inclusion of the µCT data for each scan by thresholding above 1,200 and region filling.
Generate a spreadsheet with the measured fluorescence amounts.
Plot the measured fluorescence amounts as a function of known probe amounts.
Compute the slope of a linear regression fit from the plot.
Use the computed slope as the calibration factor for the probe.
